research_question: Which candidate distributions does the frozen original public DrivoR scorer rank and calibrate reliably, and does distance from its own proposals explain errors?
notes: Reuse every trajectory and official PDMS from the previous 64-scene development panel; no new trajectory generation or evaluator calls.
Operational comparison uses four separate full 64-candidate contexts, with the same original scorer and its own frozen observation cache.
The second protocol scores all 256 identical candidates together, holding candidate attention context fixed for conditional error analysis.
Family labels follow the official family_mix generator's concatenation order, not inferred scene semantics.
Geometry and native-distance bins are descriptive analyses fixed before this run; they do not prove the training density or OOD membership.
All later score-band/safety stratification uses oracle labels for retrospective diagnosis and is not an inference-time classifier.
